human_tolerance.notes: The article calls it a bird that 'readily adapts to urban and rural environments' and 'a familiar sound in most areas of Japan', and records it invading orchards and gardens for fruit; in Tokyo it is one of the commonest garden birds.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds April to July and sometimes August; a cup nest 1.5-4.5 m up.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Northern and highland birds move south and form large winter flocks; lowland birds are resident.

vocalizations.description: Loud squeaking 'shreep' and 'weesp' calls given year round, often by flocks; the article calls the song 'one of the most unattractive noises made by any bird'.
Noisy squeaking contact call of feeding and moving flocks.
Harsh, grating alarm note given when a flock is disturbed.

external.note: gbif_usage_key 7342055 from the GBIF species match; inat_taxon_id 144910 from the iNaturalist taxa API (active, rank species, preferred common name 'Brown-eared Bulbul'); wikidata Q10770477 from the English Wikipedia page's wikibase item.

range.note: Native range from the Distribution and habitat section: the Russian Far East including Sakhalin (RU), northeastern China (CN), the Korean Peninsula (KR, KP), Japan (JP), Taiwan (TW) and the Babuyan and Batanes island chains in the north of the Philippines (PH). Country codes are a derivation from that prose.

traits.note: Mass 65 g is the midpoint of the Japanese article's 60-70 g. Length 28 cm is the English article's 'about 28 cm'; the Japanese article gives about 30 cm, so the two differ by 2 cm. Locomotion Hop is a judgement: the species feeds on fruit and insects in trees and on the ground and is not described walking, and Hop is carried from the congener records. Diet is derived from the Japanese article, which says it is omnivorous but strongly plant-eating outside summer, favouring fruit and also taking insects; fruit 0.5, invertebrate 0.3, nectar 0.2. Lifespan is not given by any source; 5 years is a judgement for a medium-sized passerine. No open source states a wingspan either, so wingspan_m 0.38 is derived by scaling the congener records in this repository by body length (0.36 m for the 0.2625 m blackbird, scaled to 0.28 m), a judgement with Low confidence.

habitat.note: The article describes a bird of forest edges, orchards, parks and gardens that nests in a cup 1.5-4.5 m up and feeds on fruit and insects, so arboreal 0.7 / ground 0.3 and shelter in shrub thickets. Resource tags follow that diet and the cup nest. human_tolerance follows the quoted adaptation to urban and rural environments.

seasonal.note: Breeds April to July, sometimes August (cup nest, about five eggs); northern and highland birds migrate south and form winter flocks while lowland birds are resident, so the strategy is ActiveYearRound with a breeding and a flocking phase. Juvenile duration is a judgement.

vocalizations.note: The English article describes 'noisy squeaking calls', loud 'shreep' and 'weesp' flock calls, and calls the song 'one of the most unattractive noises made by any bird'; the Japanese article derives the name from the 'hīyo, hīyo' call. The three calls here are a judgement mapping those descriptions onto the program's song, contact and alarm slots.

look.note: Plumage from the Description: greyish-brown with brown cheeks ('brown ears') and a long tail. The modelled cheek box carries the brown cheek patch; proportions and palette are judgement for a slim, long-tailed bulbul.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: food_tag fruit follows the strongly frugivorous diet, song and alarm are bound to the shreep and harsh alarm calls, nest months bracket the April-August breeding season and must include 4 and 5.
